title: The Tunguska Event
subtitle: The sky exploded
yt_title: The Explosion That Flattened 80 Million Trees 💥 | Ep. 110 #shorts
description:
Episode 110 of a daily journey through the universe. 💥
We go to Siberia, June 30, 1908: a space rock exploded in the air over Tunguska, flattening about 2,150 square kilometers of forest and around 80 million trees, with an energy of roughly 3 to 15 megatons, and no crater left behind.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 111: Next stop, DART. The day humans moved an asteroid.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #tunguska #astronomy #shorts #science #nasa

segments.text: Episode one hundred and ten. Next stop... the Tunguska event.
June thirtieth, nineteen oh eight. Morning in Siberia. A fireball streaks across the sky.
segments.headline: June 30, 1908

segments.text: Then, a blast. People sixty kilometers away were knocked off their feet, and felt heat like their shirts were on fire.
segments.headline: Felt 60 km away

segments.text: A space rock, maybe fifty to sixty meters wide, exploded several kilometers above the ground.
The blast flattened about two thousand one hundred and fifty square kilometers of forest. About eighty million trees.
Its energy was hundreds of times stronger than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.
When scientists finally reached the site in nineteen twenty-seven, they found something strange. No crater.
segments.headline: No crater

segments.text: Trees at the center were still standing, stripped bare. The rock blew apart in the air, before it could hit.
segments.headline: Trees standing at the center

segments.text: June thirtieth is now Asteroid Day, to remind us to watch the sky.
segments.headline: Asteroid Day

segments.text: Tomorrow, the day humans fought back. We crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid, and changed its orbit. Follow, so you don't miss episode one hundred and eleven.
